items.title: Charles Calello interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 21, 2025
items.q: Vinnie Bell, who was one of the guitar players on the session said, “Charlie, you’ve got five minutes.

ctx.x: No. In fact when I made that record – I’ll back up a couple of beats – Sandy Linzer wrote the song with Denny Randell. Sandy Linzer also wrote “Dawn (Go Away)” with Bob Gaudio, and he became one of the writers of the Four Seasons. My father actually introduced me to him. So after they had a couple of hit records with Bob Crewe they

decided to produce a record on their own. So I would sit with them and they would play me the song and then I would write the arrangements while they were sitting there. And what was interesting about it was we worked on the arrangements together. But now I did something that I didn’t realize I did. On the introduction where it started with the concerto [scats] – right after that I wrote the intro to “Stop In The Name of Love.” What was it – and unconsciously I wrote it because it went like this [scats]. And when…
It’s curious, it’s one of the few – there’s a very short list of pop tunes that have titles that are never said in the lyrics.
